t: Knowledge Organization Auditor: a plain-language overview
title: Knowledge Organization Auditor: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Knowledge Organization Auditor does and why archives need it. A knowledge organization auditor inspects the archive the way a building inspector inspects a house: it checks that every record sits in the right category, that no category contradicts itself, and that nothing is orphaned or duplicated. It reports every problem with its location, so curators can fix them one by one.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Knowledge Organization Auditor works
title: How the Knowledge Organization Auditor works
description: Overview: what the Knowledge Organization Auditor does and why archives need it. Real auditors run schema validation (required fields present, values in range), orphan detection (records pointing to deleted categories, categories with no records), and coherence checks (a 'mammal' category containing a fish is flagged by out-of-vocabulary scoring against sibling records). Duplicate and near-duplicate detection finds records filed twice, and cross-field consistency rules catch contradictions like a birth date after a death date. Findings are ranked by severity with exact record IDs attached.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Knowledge Organization Auditor works: the deep tour
title: How the Knowledge Organization Auditor works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Knowledge Organization Auditor does and why archives need it. Real auditors run schema validation (required fields present, values in range), orphan detection (records pointing to deleted categories, categories with no records), and coherence checks (a 'mammal' category containing a fish is flagged by out-of-vocabulary scoring against sibling records). Duplicate and near-duplicate detection finds records filed twice, and cross-field consistency rules catch contradictions like a birth date after a death date. Findings are ranked by severity with exact record IDs attached. Advanced auditors learn per-category norms so unusual-but-correct records are not flagged, track audit history to show whether the archive is getting cleaner over time, and distinguish structural problems (broken hierarchy) from content problems (wrong labels). Quality is measured by finding precision on seeded-error corpora — the auditor must catch planted mistakes without drowning curators in false alarms. The limits are subjective categorization disputes, which the auditor reports as curator-decision rather than error.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
